findings.claim: A company is designing a new range of outdoor garden chairs ... '12 marks - Extended'; the scheme credits 'spelling/grammar: accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar throughout'.
findings.truth: The written paper is 2 hours and 100 marks. The specialist section is worth 30 marks and holds several short answers of 2-5 marks plus one extended response; no 12-mark item sits in that section, and the specification allocates no marks anywhere for spelling, punctuation and grammar. The tariff is set to 10 marks and the bands re-cut (8-10 / 6-7 / 4-5 / 1-3) to match the fix already applied to the free-tier row of this unit.
findings.evidence: spec 2.2 Assessments (Paper 1: 2 hours, 100 marks, 50%; Section A 20 marks, Section B 30 marks with short answers 2-5 marks and one extended response, Section C 50 marks); no mention of spelling, punctuation or grammar anywhere in the specification

findings.claim: 'In AQA Design & Technology, you must understand the ecological and social issues...' and 'They appear frequently in the AQA exam and you should be able to explain each one with examples.'
findings.truth: House rule: student-facing text never names the exam board. Both sentences read the same way without the board name.
findings.evidence: house rule in the checker brief; content is bespoke school content served to students

findings.claim: Question 5 mark scheme: 'Some materials (thermosetting polymers) cannot be recycled at all.'
findings.truth: Thermosets cannot be melted down and reshaped once cured, but they are routinely ground up and used as a filler, so 'cannot be recycled at all' teaches a misconception.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Thermosetting polymer: 'Once hardened, a thermoset cannot be melted for reshaping' and 'This usually prevents recycling for the same purpose, except as filler material.'

findings.claim: Worked example: 'Good nesting reduces waste to just 40 mm × 1220 mm + 2440 mm × 20 mm of offcuts.'
findings.truth: After the 40 mm wide strip is taken off the 2440 mm length, the remaining strip is 2400 mm long, not 2440 mm. As written the 40 mm x 20 mm corner is counted twice (97,600 mm2 instead of 96,800 mm2). The panel count of 48 and both cutting figures above it recompute correctly.
findings.evidence: recomputation: 8 x 300 = 2400 mm, 6 x 200 = 1200 mm, 8 x 6 = 48 panels; offcut strips 40 x 1220 and 2400 x 20

findings.claim: Question 4 mark scheme awards the mark only for 'The paper cup company uses continuous production'.
findings.truth: Disposable paper cups are separate identical items made on automated lines, which is mass production. A student writing 'mass production' gives the better answer and would be marked wrong. The scheme now credits mass production and accepts continuous production where the candidate justifies it.
findings.evidence: spec 3.2.7 scales of production (prototype, batch, mass, continuous); continuous output such as paper reels or steel is the continuous case, the cups made from it are discrete products

findings.claim: 'The six main factors in material selection are: functionality, aesthetics, availability, cost, environmental impact, and social & ethical considerations.'
findings.truth: The specification lists eight headings for 3.2.1: functionality, aesthetics, environmental, availability, cost, social, cultural and ethical factors. The lesson folds social, cultural and ethical into one heading. Cultural factors are still taught in the body of the lesson, so nothing examinable is missing, and the 'six factors' grouping runs through the key fact, a knowledge check, a flashcard and the conclusion. Not worth an edit unless the grouping is rebuilt across all four places.
findings.evidence: spec 3.2.1 Selection of materials or components

summary: The technical content is sound: the five forces, reinforcement methods, the six Rs, sources and conversion routes, LCA stages, stock forms and standard components, the four scales of production and every finish-to-material pairing match the specification, and all 35 knowledge-check keys, the sheet-nesting example and the 133.6 m fabric calculation recompute clean. The damage is in the exam framing: all seven lessons close on a 12-mark extended response that credits spelling and grammar, neither of which exists on this paper. Lesson 3 names the board twice in student-facing prose, lesson 6's scheme marks the correct 'mass production' answer wrong, and two smaller errors (thermoset recycling, a double-counted offcut corner) are fixed.
